display.title: Episode 503: Skippy and Crawly (Kislev)
display.summary_short: Kislev's message of redemption, from Yud-Tes Kislev and Chanukah to Moshiach's clouds; Shema with a Boro Park class; and the grasshopper and the ant, about trying hard to succeed.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the middle of Kislev, before Yud-Tes Kislev. Uncle Yossi explains that Kislev brings a message of redemption and victory: on the 19th the Alter Rebbe, author of the Tanya and the Shulchan Aruch HaRav, was miraculously freed from prison, and on the 25th comes Chanukah. The greatest miracle will be the Geulah, when, as the prophet Daniel says, heavenly clouds will carry every Jew to Yerushalayim and the third Beis HaMikdash. After the Hakochainik march, a class from a Boro Park girls' school recites the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Uncle Yossi then introduces the Twelve Pesukim, especially the Sages' words 'I have toiled and I have found': success comes only through real effort, which the Torah hints at from its first verse, 'it was evening, and it was morning'. In the story, David asks why his sister Miriam always gets better marks, and his father tells him of Skippy the grasshopper, who played all summer while Crawly the ant stored food, and was left outside in the winter snow. David promises to try harder. The show ends with how to get the Twelve Pesukim booklet and the Shabbos candle-lighting times.
display.lesson: If you work hard, Hashem helps you succeed; prepare now, like the ant, instead of putting off your work.

date.note: 'Right in the middle of Kislev', with Yud-Tes Kislev still ahead; candles 4:16, Shabbos ends 5:19 fit late November 1991 in New York. One week before episode 504 (19 Kislev).

advisories.note: The Alter Rebbe's imprisonment, when his life was in danger, is mentioned briefly.
